segments.text: Site meeting number six for the future medical practice in the old bakery. We're two weeks behind on the structural work, so we need a realistic schedule by the end of this meeting.
Demolition is finished, the opening in the load-bearing wall is done and propped. The partitions for the two consulting rooms will be up by Friday, you have my word.
Théo, before we choose the basement plaster, I need a humidity reading of the walls. Can you take care of that?
Yes, I'll do the reading on Monday with the moisture meter and send you the measurements.
The doctors would like to visit at the end of November. And the neighbours are complaining about the noise, especially early in the morning.
I propose we limit noisy work to the nine-to-five window, Monday to Friday. Do you both agree?
Fine by me, the crews can live with that.
Agreed as well, the doctors approve it.
Good, so the rule applies to the whole site: noisy work from nine to five, weekdays only.
Personally, I'm switching to a tablet for my site notes, no more paper notebook. It's easier for me.
Rachid, we need the managing agent's written approval for the boiler flue outlet on the façade. Could you get it?
I won't stick my neck out on that one, the managing agent hasn't answered anyone for a month. Let's talk about the bathroom schedule instead.
Right, for the bathrooms, Rachid promised me on Monday on the phone: “I'll send you the tile choice before the end of the week.” Without it, the tiler can't order.
The plasterer just called, he can only come on Tuesday, his truck has broken down.
In that case, I'm revising what I announced: the partitions won't be up on Friday, but on Wednesday next week.
About the tiles, yes, I'm the one sending you the choice, by Friday at the latest.
Thanks. Another topic: the upstairs neighbour must be told before the slab is core-drilled, he asked for it in writing.
The core drilling is scheduled in ten days, with the rental company's machine.
Who can pick up the paint samples from the supplier?
No volunteers? Then it's on me, I'll pick them up on Tuesday at the end of the day.
And the humidity reading is pointless now, isn't it? The doctors have already gone for a lime plaster.
No, I'm keeping it. Lime or not, I need the measurements for the ten-year warranty. Théo, it's still Monday.
One last point: the town hall is still waiting for the accessibility file.
Leave that with me. The acknowledgement of receipt gives a deadline of 2026-11-27, I'll send it before that date. Thank you both, see you in a week.
